properties.title: Hammersmith, London
properties.story: The classically trained musician who joined in 1982 and became the band's studio architect through their imperial phase, from Construction Time Again to Songs of Faith and Devotion.

properties.title: South Woodford, London
properties.story: The founding songwriter behind Dreaming of Me, New Life and Just Can't Get Enough. He left after Speak & Spell to form Yazoo and later Erasure — handing the songwriting torch to Martin Gore.

properties.title: Dagenham, London
properties.story: Born in Dagenham and raised in Basildon, Martin became the band's principal songwriter from 1982 onwards — the pen behind Personal Jesus, Enjoy the Silence, Never Let Me Down Again and nearly everything else.

properties.title: Nottingham
properties.story: Born in Nottingham before his family moved to Basildon, Fletch was the band's heart, diplomat and self-described 'tall guy in the background'. He remained a constant for 42 years until his death in May 2022.

properties.title: Epping, Essex
properties.story: Born in Epping and raised in Basildon, Dave was recruited after Vince Clarke heard him sing Bowie's 'Heroes' at a jam session. He even gave the band its name, borrowed from French fashion magazine Dépêche Mode.

properties.title: Basildon, Essex
properties.story: The Essex new town where Dave Gahan, Martin Gore, Andy Fletcher and Vince Clarke grew up and formed the band in 1980. The town's pedestrian underpasses and brutalist architecture have become pilgrimage sites for fans from around the world.

trivia.curious: Basildon is a post-war 'new town' built to rehouse bombed-out Londoners.
trivia.fan: They tried the name 'Composition of Sound' before Dave Gahan suggested Depeche Mode.
trivia.devotee: Devotees still seek out the brutalist pedestrian underpasses Anton Corbijn would later echo in the band's imagery.

properties.title: Blackwing Studios, Southwark
properties.summary: The church where synth-pop history was made.
properties.story: Housed in the deconsecrated All Hallows Church in south London, Blackwing is where the first singles and the first two albums took shape — synth-pop history made inside a Victorian church.

trivia.curious: Blackwing was built inside a derelict Victorian church in Southwark.
trivia.fan: Engineer Eric Radcliffe's gear shaped the early Mute sound across Yazoo and DM alike.
trivia.devotee: The building, All Hallows, was bombed in WWII and never reconsecrated — a literal haunted box for synth-pop's birth.

properties.title: Hansa Studios, Berlin
properties.story: The band's mid-80s creative home, metres from the Berlin Wall. The Meistersaal's atmosphere — and West Berlin's nightlife — seeped into the darker, industrial textures of the band's imperial phase.

trivia.curious: Hansa Studios sits just metres from where the Berlin Wall once ran.
trivia.fan: Bowie and Iggy Pop recorded here years earlier — the 'Hansa by the Wall' mythology preceded DM.
trivia.devotee: The cavernous Meistersaal's natural reverb is all over 'Stripped' — they miked the room itself, not just the kit.

properties.title: Puk Studios, Denmark
properties.story: A residential studio in the Danish countryside where much of Violator was crafted, with Flood co-producing and Alan Wilder pushing the band's sound design to new heights.

properties.title: Madrid
properties.summary: Songs of Faith and Devotion begins.
properties.story: The band rented a villa in Madrid and converted it into a studio to begin Songs of Faith and Devotion — famously tense sessions, a band fraying at the edges, yet producing some of their most powerful music.

properties.title: Santa Barbara, California
properties.summary: The band's West Coast home base.
properties.story: From the mid-2000s, much of every album took shape in Santa Barbara, where Martin Gore settled — at Sound Design and later his home studio, wonderfully named Electric Ladyboy. The Essex boys' story now runs through Californian sunshine.

properties.title: Yazoo — Upstairs at Eric's
properties.story: Within weeks of leaving Depeche Mode, Vince Clarke was back at Blackwing with Alison Moyet recording Yazoo's debut — named after engineer Eric Radcliffe's upstairs room. Only You and Don't Go came out of the very building where Speak & Spell was made.

trivia.curious: Yazoo was Vince Clarke's duo with singer Alison Moyet.
trivia.fan: It was recorded in the same Blackwing church that birthed DM's debut.
trivia.devotee: Vince and Alison first connected through Melody Maker small ads; the album is named for Blackwing's Eric Radcliffe — 'Upstairs at Eric's'.

properties.title: The Assembly — Never Never
properties.story: Vince Clarke and Blackwing's Eric Radcliffe planned a project with a different singer on every release. They managed one: Never Never with Feargal Sharkey, a UK No. 4 — then Vince met Andy Bell and Erasure happened instead.

properties.title: Erasure forms in London
properties.story: Vince Clarke auditioned singers through a Melody Maker ad; Andy Bell was the 42nd hopeful. Wonderland followed in 1986, and Erasure became one of Britain's most enduring pop acts — still going four decades later.

properties.title: Recoil — The Thin Line, Sussex
properties.story: After leaving Depeche Mode in 1995, Alan Wilder made Recoil his full-time vehicle, recording dark, cinematic albums like Unsound Methods and subHuman at his Sussex home studio, The Thin Line.

properties.title: Martin L. Gore — Counterfeit²
properties.story: Martin's solo outlet has always been covers and instrumentals — the Counterfeit EPs and later the MG and Third Chimpanzee albums, made at his Santa Barbara home studio. The writer of hundreds of songs, relaxing in other people's.

properties.title: Dave Gahan — Paper Monsters
properties.story: Dave's solo debut, written and recorded in New York where he'd rebuilt his life. Its success changed Depeche Mode itself — from Playing the Angel onwards, Gahan songs appear on every album.

properties.title: Dave Gahan & Soulsavers
properties.story: Dave's ongoing collaboration with production duo Soulsavers — The Light the Dead See, Angels & Ghosts and Imposter — recorded largely in Los Angeles, gave his voice its most soulful setting outside the Mode.

properties.title: VCMG — Ssss
properties.story: Thirty years after Vince walked out, Clarke and Gore made a full-on techno album together for Mute — almost entirely by swapping files, barely in the same room. The most Depeche Mode reunion imaginable.

properties.title: Logic Studios, Milan
properties.story: Early in 1989 the band decamped to Milan's Logic Studios to begin Violator with producer Flood. Personal Jesus took shape here before the sessions moved north to Puk in Denmark — the first sparks of their masterpiece.

properties.title: Westside Studios, London
properties.story: Much of Black Celebration was tracked at Westside in west London before mixing at Hansa. The album where Depeche Mode fully embraced the dark — Stripped, A Question of Time, and the title-track dread that defined a generation of fans.
